EXPLANATION

The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=a is given by P4(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+f(4)(a)4!(x−a)4.

Here, we have a=0, so

P4(x)=f(0)+f′(0)x+f″(0)2!x2+f‴(0)3!x3+f(4)(0)4!x4.

So we need to work out f(0), f′(0), f″(0), f‴(0) and f(4)(0), as follows: f(x)=2e−x⟹f(0)=2e0=2f′(x)=−2e−x⟹f′(0)=−2e0=−2f″(x)=2e−x⟹f″(0)=2e0=2f‴(x)=−2e−x⟹f‴(0)=−2e0=−2f(4)(x)=2e−x⟹f(4)(0)=2e0=2

Therefore, P4(x) is given by

P4(x)=2+(−2)⋅x+22!x2+(−2)3!x3+24!x4=2−2x+x2−13x3+112x4.
